transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Meera Patel (Astoria Head of ML), Jon Ruiz (Astoria Infra Lead), Elena Kovacs (Astoria CTO)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we got about 45 minutes, quick intros? I'm Alex Chen, AE at Redwood, and Priya is our systems engineer who will dig into performance
[00:12] Meera: hi I'm Meera, lead on ML infra at Astoria, we run a mixed set of workloads, lots of streaming summarization and some batch embeddings
[00:20] Jon: Jon Ruiz, infra, we own k8s clusters and GCP infra, curious about latency and cost open to dedicated
[00:28] Elena: Elena, CTO, high-level: we need predictable p95s and data residency for EU customers
[00:35] Priya: great, goal for today is to understand your p95 targets, concurrency patterns, token lengths and whether streaming is required

[02:05] Alex: Meera, can you share current SLAs or targets? I saw in the form you indicated p95 200ms for short responses, is that correct?
[02:18] Meera: yes for short prompts ~30 tokens we want p95 under 250ms, for longer chats it's okay up to 1s but p95 consistency is key
[02:30] Jon: also we have concurrency peaks - up to 1,000 concurrent low-latency streams during peak campaign windows
[02:40] Priya: okay that's helpful. do these streams use streaming token-by-token responses (server-sent events) or do you buffer and send at end?
[02:53] Meera: streaming, token-by-token to surface partial outputs to the UI

[04:10] Priya: two paths: hosted (fastest onboarding) can hit low-ms p95 for smaller models, dedicated gives you reserved gpus for predictable throughput, private (VPC/on-prem) for strict residency. tradeoffs are cost vs control
[04:28] Alex: also we do prefix caching and intelligent batching - in many cases we can keep p95 low by caching common prefixes

[06:00] Meera: what's the typical tokens/sec throughput you'd measure? we have some requests that are 800-1,200 tokens total but 90% are under 300 tokens
[06:15] Priya: for throughput we run tokens/sec benchmarks per model and hardware. on a single nv4-s instance we get roughly 800-1.2k tokens/sec for generation at 1.6k context depending on quantization. but streaming overhead and concurrency affect p95
[06:33] Jon: can you clarify quantization impact? we prefer int8 to reduce cost
[06:40] Priya: quantization often reduces memory and can improve token/sec but sometimes hurts tail latency for short responses due to kernel selection; we test +/- bench to pick profiles

[08:05] Alex: quick note - our runtime has automatic fallback to a cheaper compatible variant when capacity constrained; that helps with graceful degradation rather than errors

[09:00] Meera: Ok, real ask: during peak we need p95 under 300ms for 90-token summaries with 1k concurrent streaming connections. is that realistic?
[09:12] Priya: 1k concurrent streaming connections with 90-token responses and p95 300ms is aggressive. we'd likely recommend Dedicated with reserved nv4 pools and tuned batching, plus prefix caching. We'll need to benchmark with your exact prompt set
[09:28] Jon: what about connection multiplexing? our k8s ingress can handle keepalives but not thousands of idle sockets
[09:36] Priya: streaming connections do need to be accounted for - we have recommendations for connection proxies and keepalive tuning; also you can use shorter-lived connections with HTTP/2 multiplexing

[11:00] Meera: for benchmarking, what artifacts do you need?
[11:06] Priya: sample prompts, representative concurrency patterns (ramp up curves), token length histograms, desired p95s per workload, and whether you use function calling/structured outputs. also any security constraints (VPC, BYOK)
[11:25] Meera: we'll share anonymized traces and the top 50 prompts

[12:05] Alex: Competitors - are you evaluating Anthropic or Bedrock?
[12:12] Elena: Yeah we have a POC with Bedrock for embeddings and also talking to Anthropic for chat. cost is a big factor
[12:22] Alex: makes sense; on pricing we typically show hosted for quick start then recommend Dedicated for predictable p95 at scale

[14:00] Priya: let me walk through a sample benchmark flow: we spin up a dedicated pool, run token/sec baseline with non-streamed requests to measure raw throughput and kernel behavior, then run streaming ramps to measure p95 and client impact. we'll instrument tracing and provide latency histograms and percentiles
[14:25] Jon: do you support real-time KV cache reuse across requests? we use prefix caching heavily
[14:33] Priya: yes, KV cache and prefix caching exist; transcription sometimes shows 'K V' but it's KV cache - we can persist KV to warm workers between requests to lower p95

[16:10] Meera: For security, we need SOC2, SAML SSO, audit logs, and KMS integration. can Redwood support HSM or customer-managed keys?
[16:26] Alex: yes SOC2 and SAML are supported, and for Private we can do customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations + VPC peering. we'll send security pack
[16:40] Elena: data residency - EU data must not leave region for some customers
[16:46] Alex: Private or Dedicated with region pinning will satisfy that; hosted can be region-limited depending on capacity

[18:10] Meera: any non-obvious tradeoffs between streaming and p95? we assume streaming adds more overhead
[18:18] Priya: streaming can increase p95 due to TCP/HTTP chunking and client-side latency; however our runtime optimizes token emission and we can tune chunk sizes and flush intervals. also batching behavior is different for streaming vs non-streaming

[20:00] Jon: about autoscale - when traffic drops, do you incur warm-up latency when scaling down and back up?
[20:09] Alex: Dedicated has configurable autoscale policies and burst capacity; we keep a warm pool to avoid cold starts and your SLOs will guide minimum pool sizes

[22:30] Priya: Pricing note - dedicated committed capacity reduces per-token cost significantly vs hosted, but there's a baseline monthly commit
[22:40] Meera: We're sensitive to cost but p95 consistency is top priority

[24:00] Alex: quick demo offer - we can run a 2 hour benchmark with your traces on dedicated and hosted to show p95/throughput diff. Priya will prepare a benchmark template
[24:12] Meera: yes let's do that. timeline: want results before next exec sync in two weeks

[26:00] Priya: I'll need your sample traces and target windows. we'll run: 1) single-node token/sec baseline, 2) multi-node concurrency ramp to 1k streams, 3) streaming token emission test, 4) end-to-end p95 histograms
[26:20] Jon: ok we'll anonymize and upload to the secure share

[28:00] Alex: a few gotchas - client-side rendering latency can dominate. you should measure end-to-end in parallel with server metrics
[28:20] Meera: noted

[30:00] Priya: technical aside: kernel selection can cause jitter at tail if model switches kernels between layers; we pin kernels for critical workloads. quantization profiles also get tested for tail behavior
[30:25] Jon: interesting - can you produce kernel-level traces?
[30:30] Priya: yes we'll include flame-like kernel timing breakdown in the benchmark results

[33:00] Meera: If we go Dedicated, what's typical sizing for 1k concurrent streams at 90 tokens p95 300ms?
[33:12] Priya: ballpark - a small fleet of nv4-s instances, likely 8-12 GPUs depending on model family and quantization. exact # depends on your prompts. we'll provide a sizing doc

[35:00] Alex: Next steps recap - Priya shares benchmark template and config; Alex will send pricing; Meera to upload traces
[35:12] Elena: can you include a security pack and SLA examples for dedicated?
[35:20] Alex: yes will attach docs and SOC2/ISO outlines

[36:00] Meera: Any red flags for private deployment? latency wise on-prem could be faster but ops complexity high
[36:12] Priya: Private gives you control but you manage networking and scaling. Redwood offers an on-prem package and a private control plane to reduce ops but still some customer work

[38:00] Jon: curious about failure modes - if a GPU node fails, do requests retry or get queued?
[38:10] Priya: we have automated request routing and fallback to alternate variants or regions; we also keep hot spares. we'll show the routing policy in docs

[40:00] Alex: Ok last question: do you need function calling and structured outputs? those affect token lengths and latency
[40:10] Meera: yes function calls for entity extraction in stream - tend to add 20-50 tokens overhead
[40:20] Priya: we'll model that in benchmarks

[42:00] Alex: Wrap up - agreed actions and schedule

[42:10] Alex: thanks everyone, we'll send summary and connect on the benchmark kickoff
[42:20] Meera: thanks, looking forward

End of transcript
